newsitem.title: USA: Conseco capable of more deals, buybacks.
newsitem.headline: Conseco capable of more deals, buybacks.

text.p: Conseco Inc said it has the financial flexibility to pursue acquisitions as large as $2 billion or buy back about $1 billion of its own stock.

Conseco Chairman Stephen Hilbert said with the current debt to capital ratio at 22 percent, well below the company's 35 percent target, and $740 million of cash flow, "we have the balance sheet flexibility we need in order to pursue the most profitable opportunities we can find."

"We can pursue additional cash acquisitions, financed with debt, as large as $2 billion; we can use our equity to accomplish strategic, accretive acquisitions; or we can buy back about $1 billion of our own stock, financed with debt, and still maintain our targeted debt/capital ratio," he said.
He said one of the company's major goals for 1997 is to continue to seek opportunities to supplement growth through strategic, accretive acquisitions.
He said the company's pending acquisition of Pioneer Financial Services is expected to close by the end of May.

Upon completion of that deal, Conseco will have about $32 billion of investments under management, $30 billion of assets on its own balance sheet, $7.3 billion of annual premiums and revenues, $9 billion of equity market capitalization, and a book value of more than $18 per share.
